children: The dollar falls to its lowest in nearly a week against a basket of currencies, helped by sharp gains in the Japanese yen amid chatter of potential intervention to prop it up after recent declines. The DXY dollar index falls to a six-day low of 99.166 as the U.S. currency drops more than 1% to a one-month low of 156.34 yen, LSEG data show. The yen's sharp jump has had "a knock-on negative impact on the dollar," ING's Francesco Pesole says in a note. Also weighing on the dollar are Wednesday's weak U.S. ADP private payrolls data and comments from New York Fed President John Williams that there is no clear evidence for now to suggest interest rates need to rise. (jessica.fleetham@wsj.com)
